stories.title: Extract the type scale into tokens.css (closes W-3) -- pure refactor
stories.completionNotes:
DONE (commit f48b3c6). 82 bare `font-size: Npx` in dashboard.css -> 5 scale tokens declared in tokens.css and mirrored into dashboard.css :root (the mirror is the established pattern -- dashboard.html links ONLY dashboard.css, so an SSOT-only drop would leave the panel unsized with a green suite; BL-027 lesson). Values are the PRE-F-127 shipped scale: hero 40 / primary 20 / secondary 14 / label 12 / meta 10. US-540-a sets 44/34/26/20/15 by editing the SSOT + the mirror -- nothing below :root changes again.

*** ONE DEVIATION, RATIFY BEFORE CLOSING THE SPRINT -- filed as offices/pm/issues/I-us539-type-scale-collapse-is-not-pixel-identical.md. AC3 asks for BOTH five tokens AND 'renders visually identical'. The file shipped 15 DISTINCT sizes (8/9/10/11/12/13/14/15/17/18/20/22/30/34/40); 15 values do not fit in 5 slots, so the two clauses are mutually exclusive on this file. I took the COLLAPSE, because the pixel-identical alternative (5 tokens + ~10 extra tokens holding the off-scale sizes) BREAKS US-540-a: that story is specified as setting FIVE values, and would leave ten stale -- the 'edits that drift' problem, just smaller. Every off-scale rule rounds UP to its tier, so NOTHING on the panel got smaller. Moves: 34/30/22->hero(3 rules), 18/17/15->primary(6), 13->secondary(21), 11->label(14), 9/8->meta(3); the other 35 rules already sat on a scale value. The one call worth Iris's eye: the STOP takeover directive goes 22->40 -- forced, because Spool 6d requires it outrank its base rule (.takeover-directive, which landed on primary), and a collapse onto one tier would have turned a SAFETY guard red. 'PULL OVER NOW' at 40px mono is ~340px of the 442px available; fits on paper, EYEBALL IT ON THE PI when US-540-a re-verifies (which raises hero to 44). ***

TWO PRE-EXISTING SAFETY GUARDS read font sizes with a raw-px regex (test_dashboard_stop_tier_safety::test_stopTakeover_directiveIsLargerThanBaseCopy, test_dtc_detail_hierarchy::test_directiveBand_isLargerThanTheDetailBodyBaseCopy). Tokenizing would have left them reading 'size absent' -- one dies on a None match, the other silently compares -1. A refactor that blinds a safety guard is worse than the drift it fixed. Both now resolve var(--fs-*) through the scale via ONE shared helper, tests/ui/css_type_scale.py, which also carries the LINE-ANCHORED ruleBlock(): a plain substring search for '.takeover-directive {' finds the STOP OVERRIDE first (declared earlier in the sheet), so a naive guard compares the override against ITSELF and reports a hierarchy that does not exist. My first cut had exactly that bug and the new test caught it (40 <= 40) -- the pre-existing suite had already solved it, which is why only my new test went red.

NEW GATE tests/ui/test_dashboard_type_scale.py (17 tests). Every assertion is an ABSENCE check, so it ships with a NEGATIVE CONTROL: the bare-px detector is driven against a stylesheet that DOES carry drift and must report it, and against a `--fs-hero: 40px` declaration it must NOT. Without the pair, a typo in the pattern reads as a green gate over a file full of literals. Also gated: font-size right-hand sides are ONLY a scale token or the deliberate `inherit` on .detail-value (US-491 load-bearing -- binding a token there re-breaks the tier ramp and looks tidier doing it); no SIXTH --fs-* token (sprawl comes back one token at a time); scale strictly descending (survives US-540-a by asserting ORDER not numbers).

GATE RUN SYNCHRONOUSLY: tests/ui/ ALL 720 passed. ruff clean on 4 touched .py. PM: this touches a SHARED stylesheet + 2 existing test files, so tests/ui/ is worth the integration re-run; no src/ or Python runtime code touched, so the wider suite is low-risk. GOTCHA FOR THE NEXT AGENT: a comment containing the literal string '@import' fails test_dashboard_brand_font_payload + test_dashboard_fidelity_pass -- both scan the raw text for it (offline-kiosk guard, correctly). I reworded the comment; do NOT weaken the guard.

replace the ~83 hardcoded `font-size: Npx` in dashboard.css with token refs; DoD: NO bare `font-size: Npx` left in dashboard.css (a grep gate)

stories.completionNotes:
*** CLOSED 2026-08-11 BY US-541-a -- passes flipped false -> true. Everything below was written when AC-3 was blocked and is preserved as the record; read it as history, not as current state. AC-3's resolver defect (BL-031 / I-us536) is FIXED: Atlas Option-1 was ratified by the CIO, built as US-541-a in this same sprint, and the strict xfail this story left behind (test_resolveCarouselConfig_honoursTheShippedOffValue) is now a normal green assertion with the marker deleted -- exactly the signal it was written to give. autoRotateS:0 now survives resolveCarouselConfig, so the shipped OFF value reaches the panel. THE FINDING BELOW WAS THE RIGHT DELIVERABLE: refusing to overrule my own open escalation is what got the tie-break made by the role that owns it, one sprint later and one line long. The ONE thing this story still owes is its own in-car read (parked Home face + 'carousel does not auto-advance'), batched with the rest of the sprint's hardware reads after US-552. ***

--- ORIGINAL NOTES (written while AC-3 was blocked) ---

PARTIAL -- passes:false ON AC-3 ALONE. AC-1 (IMU-always-on) and AC-2 (reorder) are DONE, gated and committed; AC-3 ran its verification and the verification FAILED against a pre-existing open defect that needs an Atlas ruling. Filed offices/pm/blockers/BL-031-us541-ac3-autorotate-off-is-inert-resolver-rejects-zero.md.

*** AC-3 IS THE WHOLE BLOCK, AND THE STORY'S OWN PREMISE IS FALSE. The AC says autoRotateS:0 'ALREADY landed via US-536/disposition-B; this story just VERIFIES it holds.' IT DID NOT LAND. config.json ships 0; resolveCarouselConfig (carousel.js:218) admits an override only when `v > 0`, so 0 is DISCARDED and CAROUSEL_DEFAULTS restores 8s. The carousel still rotates every 8 seconds on the panel, US-533's operator toggle writes exactly the value the resolver drops (a silent no-op in the band built to make silent no-ops impossible), and US-536's disposition-B freeze fix is inert while the GPU flag it was chosen INSTEAD OF is gone. Already filed 2026-08-10 as I-us536-shipped-autorotates-zero-is-rejected-by-resolver.md; US-541 is the first story whose ACCEPTANCE depends on it, hence the escalation to a blocker. I did NOT fix it: the one-line fix inverts a deliberate US-506 invariant (the guard exists so a misconfiguration cannot silently kill the carousel) against a deliberate US-536 choice (0 = kill it on purpose) -- same value, opposite meanings, both intentional, so the tie-break is Atlas's per the role boundary. Filing an escalation last sprint and overruling it this sprint because it is inconvenient is the exact drift the refusal rules exist to prevent. Option 1 in the issue is still right and is now cheaper than it reads: I pinned GREEN that shouldAutoAdvance + rotateProgress ALREADY treat 0 as OFF, so it really is one line at the resolver with nothing downstream to follow. ***

AC-1 AS BUILT: homeFace(imuData, sysData, nowMs) -> homeFace(imuData, nowMs). US-508 let parked WIN OUTRIGHT, which hid the one instrument that is Pi-local and always-live at precisely the moment its readings are both true and worth looking at. DROPPING THE PARAMETER IS THE GUARD, not a tidy-up: a function that cannot SEE system-status cannot re-couple the home face to it, so a future re-coupling has to widen the signature first -- a visible act rather than a condition slipped into the body. carouselIdle keeps its OTHER consumers (auto-rotate pause, home-nav edge) untouched, which is also what US-542's AC-4 will want to pin.

THE SUBTLE HALF, AND IT IS THE PART THAT COULD HAVE SHIPPED A LIE: renderHome passed `face.parked ? null : face.reason` into idleCardView so the calm STANDBY hero could show when parked. With parked no longer a route to the idle face, that ternary is ALWAYS FALSE -- so it would have quietly handed a DEAD SENSOR the 'engine off - OBD asleep' hero. That is precisely the fabrication US-508's own section-2 tests were written to prevent, arriving through the back door of a condition that no longer means anything. The reason is now passed unconditionally, and homeFace returns NO `parked` field at all (pinned) so no renderer can branch on a verdict nothing computes.

AC-1's typed-NA half needed NO new code -- gear (level 'unavailable', value '--', reason beside it) and altitude (naTile -> 'NA') were already honest, and dashboard.css already greys [data-level="unavailable"] (lines 332/413). What CHANGED is that those tiles are now reachable on a PARKED bench, which was previously an unreachable state, so I gated them there. Gated with them, and this is the fact US-542's whole retirement argument rests on: a TRUE 0.0 g renders as a MEASURED zero (available, dot at the origin) while an ABSENT g renders as unavailable with NO dot -- shipped as a pair, because 'zero draws a dot at the origin' is also satisfied by a card that draws an origin dot for a dead accelerometer, and then absence and measured-zero look identical on the glass.

AC-2 VERIFIED, NOT RE-DONE (as my Sprint-74 handoff said): the order landed with US-540-b's 6-card pass. Pinned here as an ORDERED PREFIX (Home . Alerts . System Status) rather than a membership check -- a set-or-count assertion goes green on a carousel that opens on Light.

WATCH THIS IN THE REGRESSION: FOUR of the six US-508 homeFace tests went red, and the OTHER TWO went green FOR THE WRONG REASON -- with the middle argument dropped, `_view('homeFace', imu, sys, ts)` binds sys as nowMs, so those two passed with a dict for a clock. I repointed all six, not just the red four. A dropped parameter turns every stale 3-arg call site into a silently mis-bound one, and only the tests that actually USE the clock (the stale-feed one) go red to tell you.

GATE RUN SYNCHRONOUSLY IN-LOOP: tests/ui + tests/deploy/test_dashboard_kit.py = 790 collected, 790 passed (789 + 1 xfail), exit 0, zero F/E. That fence, not tests/ui alone -- US-540-b's lesson, since this touches shipped dist/ code. Baseline was 774; +17 new, -1 net from the six-into-five homeFace repoint. ruff clean on both touched .py. No src/ or Python runtime code touched.

STILL OWED ON HARDWARE (AC-1's own validationCriteria, not closable on the dev box): park the Pi engine-off and confirm the Home face shows the LIVE IMU instrument -- real heading, a real 0.0 g -- with gear/altitude greyed-NA. Read it AFTER US-552 pins the output mode, with the US-540 in-car reads.

stories.title: Resolver honours autoRotateS:0 as a real OFF value (unblocks US-541 AC-3 / BL-031)
stories.goal: As the operator, I want auto-rotate OFF to actually stay off, so the CIO freeze fix and the F-126 Settings 'Off' toggle are not silent no-ops.

the US-506 misconfig-guard intent is preserved for every key except autoRotateS: a non-number / NaN / Infinity / negative autoRotateS still falls back to the default (only a clean 0 is admitted).

conditionalOutcomes: Per-key relaxation only. If a future key legitimately needs 0-as-value, it opts in the same way -- do NOT widen the shared guard.
stories.completionNotes:
DONE, all five ACs. The relaxation is a NAMED PER-KEY ALLOW-LIST, not a loosened comparison: `var ZERO_IS_A_VALUE = { autoRotateS: true }` sits above resolveCarouselConfig and gates the one ratified key; the guard is now `if (typeof v !== 'number' || !isFinite(v)) continue;` then `if (v > 0 || (v === 0 && zeroOk)) out[key] = v;`. NaN / Infinity / negative / non-number are still rejected for EVERY key INCLUDING autoRotateS -- a NaN period makes `sinceMs >= autoRotateS * 1000` permanently false, i.e. the same silent freeze from a value nobody chose, which is precisely what US-506 refused. Only a CLEAN 0, only where 0 was given a meaning.

*** WHY THE ALLOW-LIST AND NOT `>= 0` ON autoRotateS, SINCE THE TWO ARE INDISTINGUISHABLE TODAY: with one opt-in key they agree on every input that exists right now. They diverge on the NEXT key added to CAROUSEL_DEFAULTS -- under a relaxed comparison it silently inherits 0-as-value; under the allow-list it does not. The AC's 'per-key relaxation, NOT a blanket >= 0' is therefore unfalsifiable behaviourally at the moment it is written, so I pinned it STRUCTURALLY (the resolver body must reference ZERO_IS_A_VALUE and must not contain `>= 0`; the literal must hold only autoRotateS). conditionalOutcomes says a future key opts in the same way -- that now arrives as a RED test asking for the decision rather than a line nobody reviewed. ***

TDD RED FIRST and the red was exactly two assertions, both describing the fix: the un-markered xfail test and the new admit test, `assert 8 == 0` on each. The other two new gates were GREEN BEFORE AND AFTER on purpose -- they are the BOUND on the change, not a description of it, and a bound that was never red is still doing work as long as its mechanism is proven live (see below).

NEW GATES in tests/ui/test_carousel_nav_model.py, the resolver's own home rather than the IMU file, so the resolver contract stays in one place (4 tests): (1) THE ADMIT, with a sibling key in the SAME injected object asserted to still fall back -- otherwise a per-CALL relaxation ('this object came from config, trust all of it') passes as a per-KEY one; (2) 0 STILL REFUSED FOR EVERY OTHER KEY, iterating keys PARSED OUT OF THE SHIPPED CAROUSEL_DEFAULTS rather than a list retyped in the test -- a hand-written list is a second copy of the key set, and a key added tomorrow would go green having never been tested. NON-VACUITY IS EXPLICIT AND HAS TWO HALVES: the parse is asserted to have found autoRotateS + >=7 keys, and the test above it proves this exact call path CAN return a 0 -- so a 0 not coming back is a refusal, not a lookup that cannot see the thing (US-552's 18-vacuous-passes lesson); (3) MALFORMED VALUES on autoRotateS itself (-1, '0', null, true, [], {}) -- NaN/Infinity have no JSON literal so the probe cannot carry them, which the test says out loud and covers via the isFinite guard in the body rather than pretending; (4) the STRUCTURAL pin above.

AC-3 SATISFIED: the strict xfail marker on test_resolveCarouselConfig_honoursTheShippedOffValue is DELETED, the test kept, and its docstring rewritten to record that it shipped as a strict xfail and why that shape paid off -- it XPASSed into a normal green instead of a red reading 'the bug is expected'. Zero xfail remains in the fence (verified: no 'x' anywhere in the progress output).

stories.title: Pin Pi HDMI/KMS output to the panel-native 480x320 (kill downsampling)
stories.completionNotes:
DONE deploy-side. *** COMMIT OWED -- BL-032's stale .git/index.lock is STILL unclearable (mtime 10:54, size unchanged at ~80 min; `rm` refused as a sensitive-path write in BOTH Bash and PowerShell, `Get-Process` not even on the allow-list so the holder cannot be enumerated). This is the SECOND consecutive iteration to finish green and be unable to commit, so the loop is stopped with HUMAN_INTERVENTION_REQUIRED rather than bank a third. The four files are on disk and green; BL-032 carries the exact two-commit recipe, cleanly separable by path from US-542's nine. ***

*** THE ONE DESIGN CALL WORTH ATLAS'S EYE, BECAUSE IT INVERTS A DELIBERATE US-524 REFUSAL: this script writes to /boot/firmware/cmdline.txt -- the file set-gpu-cma.sh explicitly refuses to touch, with a test (test_setGpuCma_neverWritesCmdlineTxt) pinning the refusal. That refusal was RIGHT for its job (CMA had a config.txt mechanism; a bad overlay param costs a dark display with SSH alive, a corrupted cmdline.txt costs `root=` on a Pi that lives in a car). The output mode has NO such alternative on a Pi 5: the legacy config.txt hdmi_group/hdmi_mode/hdmi_cvt path is Pi 4-and-earlier firmware, so the KMS `video=` kernel arg is the only boot-level lever. I bounded the risk instead of avoiding it, and the four interlocks ARE the deliverable as much as the pin is: (1) the connector is DISCOVERED from /sys/class/drm, never assumed -- a Pi 5 has two micro-HDMI ports and pinning the empty one is a silent no-op that still prints 'applied'; (2) nothing is written unless EXACTLY ONE connector reads `connected` (no panel on a bench deploy, or two panels, means we cannot know the target and a guess is a confident wrong answer); (3) THE TARGET MODE MUST BE ONE THE PANEL ITSELF ADVERTISES in its EDID mode list; (4) the composed line is verified BEFORE install (one line, root= and every original token intact) and re-read after, with an automatic restore from the pristine backup if the post-write read disagrees. ***

*** INTERLOCK 3 IS ALSO THE STORY'S REMAINING UNCERTAINTY, AND I LEFT IT AS A REFUSAL ON PURPOSE. If the panel does NOT advertise 480x320 -- which is a live possibility and arguably the very reason the Pi negotiates 1080p in the first place -- the script WARNs, prints what the panel does advertise, and pins NOTHING. Forcing a CVT-generated timing the panel never claimed can scan out black, in a car, with no local recovery; that is not a call to make from a Windows box that cannot read the panel's EDID. So the deploy turns the unknown into a precise machine-produced finding on its next run rather than a guess. If that WARN fires, it is an Atlas/A-16 EDID finding, not a bug in this script. ***

HOW AC-1's 'read the actual output mode' WAS SATISFIED WITHOUT A PI: I cannot reach the Pi from this harness (ping/ssh are not on the allow-list, and every prior Sprint-74 session recorded the same). So the read is IMPLEMENTED rather than performed -- the deploy step reads it on the Pi, every time, and reports it. Source is /sys/class/graphics/fb0/virtual_size, deliberately NOT kmsprint/xrandr as the AC's parenthetical suggests: neither is installed on this Pi (kmsprint ships with libdrm-tests, xrandr is X11-only and would read the session rather than the scanout), whereas the sysfs read needs no package and no X. When it is unreadable the script prints 'unknown' rather than inventing a mode -- honest-instrument, and scenario 14 pins it.

DELIBERATE DEVIATION FROM THE AC'S CONDITIONAL, FLAGGED: the AC says pin 'if it is NOT native' and conditionalOutcomes calls an already-native Pi 'a no-op verification'. I PIN UNCONDITIONALLY (idempotently) and report the observed mode alongside. Reason: an EDID negotiation that happened to land native at THIS boot is not a guarantee for the next one -- a cable resat, a cold panel, an OS image update and it re-negotiates -- and the DoD's own words are 'deploy SETS the output mode'. Skipping the write on a lucky boot leaves the durable guarantee unbuilt. Where the mode is already native the pin changes nothing visible, which is exactly the no-op outcome the story anticipates; what it removes is the luck.

EXIT-CODE CONTRACT IS LOAD-BEARING AND GATED (test_setDisplayMode_neverExitsNonZeroOnADeliberateNoOp): deploy-pi.sh runs under `set -e`, so ANY non-zero exit halts the whole deploy. Every 'did not pin' path therefore exits 0 with a loud WARN -- a bench Pi with no panel attached is not a deploy failure. Non-zero is reserved for a malformed boot cmdline (1) and a failed write (2), both of which MUST stop the deploy before anyone reboots. The guard asserts the declared codes are exactly {0,1,2}, so a later edit cannot introduce a third code that turns an unplugged panel into a halted deploy. Note set-gpu-cma.sh's exit 3 does exactly that -- correct for its case (a broken boot config), wrong for this one.

NEW GATES: tests/deploy/test_set_display_mode.sh (14 scenarios, 50 assertions) + tests/deploy/test_set_display_mode.py (9 tests: the catalog runner plus the wiring guards bash cannot express). TDD RED FIRST -- the catalog ran before the script existed and reported 18 passed / 32 failed. THOSE 18 VACUOUS PASSES ARE WORTH THE NEXT AGENT'S ATTENTION: they are the 'file NOT modified' / 'no backup written' absence assertions, which all pass trivially when the script does not exist at all. Every refusal scenario therefore ALSO asserts a positive -- the exit code and specific WARN content -- because a safety interlock proven only by 'nothing happened' is proven by nothing.

THE PYTHON GUARD I'D KEEP IF I COULD KEEP ONLY ONE: test_setDisplayMode_defaultTargetMatchesTheDocumentedPanelResolution parses the 480x320 out of docs/hardware-reference.md's panel spec table and asserts the script's default equals IT -- not a second copy of the literal in the test. Swap the panel and the guard goes red instead of the deploy quietly pinning 480x320 at a screen that is no longer 480x320. Also gated: no hard-coded HDMI-A-N anywhere in executable lines (comments stripped first -- the header discusses the ports at length), and root= is checked in CODE, not merely promised in prose.

GATE RUN SYNCHRONOUSLY IN-LOOP: full tests/deploy/ = 453 collected, 453 passed, exit 0, zero F/E. That fence and not just the new file, because this edits deploy-pi.sh, which a dozen other tests parse. ruff clean on the new .py. No src/ or Python runtime code touched; no UI file touched (US-542's uncommitted UI work sits alongside untouched).

STILL OWED ON HARDWARE, and it is the whole of AC-2 -- NOT closable on the dev box, and it is the story's actual acceptance: deploy, then reboot, then read the mode on the Pi (`cat /sys/class/graphics/fb0/virtual_size` expects 480,320) and LOOK at a card. WATCH THE DEPLOY OUTPUT ITSELF FIRST -- if the step WARNs 'does not advertise 480x320', the pin did not happen and the EDID finding is the result. ORDERING: US-540-a's AC2 says the 44/34/26/20/15 values may not be called final until this mode is confirmed native, so this read gates the in-car type-scale ratify, and both should happen on the same visit with US-541's and US-542's parked reads.

If it is NOT the panel's native 480x320, PIN the output to native in the deploy (KMS/HDMI mode). stories.title: index_lock preflight clears a STABILITY-VERIFIED non-empty stale lock (BL-032 self-heal)
stories.goal: As the loop, I want the ralph.sh preflight to self-heal the crashed-mid-write lock (a full index copy left behind), so a non-empty stale lock stops halting the sprint and needing a manual PM clear.
acceptance: [BL-032 root cause] offices/pm/scripts/index_lock.py refuses ONLY 0-byte locks today (DEFAULT_MAX_STALE_SIZE_BYTES=0, REFUSED_NONEMPTY). BL-032's lock was 376467 bytes -- a crashed `git` wrote the whole index into index.lock then died before the atomic rename -> a non-empty ORPHAN the preflight cannot clear. Add a two-sample STABILITY probe: sample (st_size, st_mtime_ns) twice separated by a short settle interval; a non-empty lock is admitted as orphaned ONLY when BOTH samples are byte-identical AND age > threshold AND no live git process. Rationale: a real mid-write index changes size/mtime between samples in well under 1s; a lock stable across the interval is not being written.

the existing fail-safes stay intact and FIRST: live-git-process gate unchanged (refuse), too-fresh gate unchanged (refuse), probe-failure => assume-live => refuse. A non-empty lock whose two samples DIFFER stays REFUSED_NONEMPTY (still mid-write). Only a *stable* non-empty lock becomes clearable.

new LockDecision path + message distinguishes 'cleared: verified-stale EMPTY' from 'cleared: verified-stale STABLE non-empty (2 samples identical, age Ns, no git)'. --check dry-run reports the same verdict without deleting.

settle interval + require-stability are parameters (injectable for tests, sane default ~1.5-2s); wire the CLI/preflight to enable stability-clearing so `python -m offices.pm.scripts.index_lock --repo <root>` in ralph.sh:237 now heals this case.

TDD: tests cover (a) stable non-empty aged no-git => CLEARED; (b) non-empty but size/mtime changes between samples => REFUSED_NONEMPTY; (c) live git => REFUSED_GIT_LIVE even if stable; (d) too-fresh => REFUSED_TOO_FRESH; (e) empty aged => CLEARED (regression, unchanged). ruff/mypy clean, coverage holds.

validationCriteria.action: simulate BL-032: a 376467-byte index.lock, mtime 80min old, no git process, size stable across two samples; run the preflight
validationCriteria.outcome: preflight CLEARS it and reports the stable-non-empty path; a lock whose size changes between samples is still refused

conditionalOutcomes: Standing risk (BL-032): Ralph's clone still lives on the shared NAS path -- this self-heal removes the STOP condition but not the contention. The durable fix (finish Ralph's clone move off the NAS) stays open, routed to CIO.
stories.completionNotes:
DONE, all five ACs. The guard now asks the question SIZE CANNOT ANSWER. BL-032's lock and a live mid-write index are indistinguishable by size -- both are big -- so a size-only rule had to refuse both, and refusing cost the sprint two uncommitted stories plus a manual PM clear. The new evidence is CHANGE OVER TIME: sample (st_size, st_mtime_ns), wait the settle interval, sample again. Identical => nothing is writing it => a crashed orphan. Different => a live writer => still REFUSED_NONEMPTY.

*** THE ONE THING I ADDED THAT THE AC DID NOT ASK FOR, AND IT IS A SAFETY HOLE THE STORY WOULD OTHERWISE HAVE OPENED: the settle interval is a ~1.5s WINDOW THAT DID NOT EXIST BEFORE. The pre-US-554 guard probed git once and deleted immediately; now there is real time between the probe and the unlink, so a git process can START inside it and be live at the moment we delete. AC-2 says the live-git gate is 'unchanged', and unchanged code would have been a regression here -- the gate is the same, but what it guards moved. The invariant is re-asserted AFTER the settle, pinned by test_clearStaleIndexLock_gitAppearsDuringSettle_refusesGitLive, which also asserts probes==2 so it cannot pass by simply never re-probing. GENERALIZE: when you introduce a WAIT between a check and the action it authorizes, the check has to be re-run -- a time-of-check/time-of-use gap is created by adding latency, not only by adding code. ***

GATE ORDER IS UNCHANGED AND PINNED BOTH WAYS: git-live first, too-fresh second, stability last. The two refusal tests also assert the settle was NEVER ENTERED (settled == []), which pins the ORDER, not just the outcome -- a rearrangement that let a too-fresh lock reach the probe would still return REFUSED_TOO_FRESH and go green on an outcome-only assertion, while quietly having paid 1.5s and, worse, having put a fresh lock on a code path that can delete. The empty-lock path likewise never settles, so the common preflight case costs nothing.

THE PAIR, NOT THE SIZE: the probe compares (size, mtime_ns) TOGETHER. A writer rewriting the same byte count slips past a size-only compare; a coarse-granularity filesystem can hide a same-second mtime move that the size reveals. Both directions are gated, and the mtime test sets mtime EXPLICITLY via os.utime rather than by touching the file, so it does not depend on the share's clock granularity to fail. The 'still changing' tests drive the change through the REAL FILESYSTEM from inside the injected settleSleep -- which is exactly what a live writer does from the guard's point of view -- rather than stubbing stat.

TWO EXISTING TESTS WERE REPOINTED, NOT DELETED, AND THAT IS THE HONEST RECORD OF WHAT CHANGED: test_clearStaleIndexLock_nonEmptyLock_refusesAndKeepsLock and test_backoff_nonEmpty_isTerminalNoSpin both planted a STATIC non-empty lock and asserted refusal -- i.e. they pinned precisely the behaviour US-554 exists to remove. They now plant a GROWING lock. The refusal survives; what changed is that it keys on change, not on size. A story that flips a pinned behaviour should move the pin and say so, never quietly delete the test.

DEFAULT IS ON (allowStableNonEmpty=True) in BOTH the library and the CLI, with --no-stable-nonempty as the opt-out. The AC only required the CLI to heal without new flags, but a library default that disagrees with its own CLI is how the next caller gets surprised; the blast radius is bounded because ralph.sh is the ONLY caller in the tree (checked, not assumed -- `git grep -l index_lock -- '*.py' '*.sh'` returns the module, its tests, and ralph.sh). Note the settle sleep is injected as settleSleep, NOT sleep: clearStaleIndexLockWithBackoff already owns `sleep` for its retry ladder and does not forward it, so reusing the name would have silently bound the backoff sleep to the settle.

*** AC-4 WAS THE ONLY AC THAT COULD HAVE SHIPPED UNFALSIFIABLE, so I gated the WIRING as well as the unit: nothing in the tree asserted that ralph.sh still CALLS this module. Delete the preflight line and all 33 unit tests stay green while the loop receives no fix at all -- US-540-b's lesson one layer up. test_ralphShPreflight_invokesTheGuardWithStabilityClearingEnabled strips comments FIRST (the preflight is documented in a long comment block that also names the module, so an unstripped scan finds the module name in PROSE and reports wiring that is not there), asserts the invocation was FOUND before judging its shape, and asserts it does not pass --no-stable-nonempty. ***

NEW LockDecision.CLEARED_STABLE_NONEMPTY (AC-3), included in safeToProceed, absent from _WAITABLE. The two cleared messages are asserted DISTINCT and to carry their evidence: a PM reading the preflight line needs to know whether the guard removed a 0-byte nothing or a 376kB index copy -- those warrant different follow-up. Also handled: the lock VANISHING mid-settle (a finishing git renamed it away) returns ABSENT rather than raising -- the happy version of mid-write, and the probe must not crash on a file disappearing between two stats.

TDD, RED TWICE ON PURPOSE: run 1 was an ImportError (symbol missing) which masks every per-test reason, so I added ONLY the skeleton -- constant, enum member, inert parameters -- and re-ran to get 9 BEHAVIOURAL reds, each failing because the probe was absent rather than because a name was. The other new tests were green before and after by design: they are the BOUND on the change (refusals that must survive it), not descriptions of it. Their non-vacuity is carried by the headline test, which proves this exact call path CAN return CLEARED_STABLE_NONEMPTY -- so a refusal is a refusal, not a lookup that cannot see the thing.

*** MYPY WAS NOT RUN -- IT IS NOT INSTALLED IN THIS ENVIRONMENT (`No module named mypy`), the same class of gap as `make` not being on PATH. AC-5 asks for mypy clean and I will not report a tool clean that I could not execute. Note CLAUDE.md scopes typechecking to `mypy src/`, and this file is under offices/, so it is likely outside the configured surface anyway -- PM to confirm at integration. RUFF IS CLEAN on both touched .py (exit 0). ***

PRE-EXISTING RED FOUND AND FILED, NOT FIXED -- TD-081: tests/pm/test_prd_to_sprint.py has TWO permanently-failing tests (KeyError 'bigDoDHash') that predate me. Commit 22f65a8 retired the freeze mechanic and stopped prd_to_sprint stamping frozenAt/bigDoDHash; the producer went, these tests stayed. Verified not mine (my diff is index_lock.py / ralph.sh / test_index_lock.py; neither the failing test nor its subject appears in it). PM-owned process scripts, so I filed rather than deleted. WORTH PM'S ATTENTION BEYOND THE TWO REDS: a standing red in tests/pm trains agents to read red as normal, and I had to spend a step proving it was not mine.

PROSE REPOINTED (my own prior lesson -- when you change a behaviour, grep for the text that described it): the module docstring's condition 3 said 'Empty (0 bytes)' full stop; ralph.sh's preflight comment said the helper 'clears ONLY a lock that is 0-byte'; the backoff docstring said a non-empty lock 'won't cure by waiting'.
